tweets.title: UN REPORT LINKS DELHI RED FORT BLAST TO AQIS A UN Security Council monitoring report has attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s Red Fort to Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), adding an international dimension to India’s investigation. The assessment says AQIS has evolved into a decentralised network of smaller cells, with leadership based in Kabul and efforts to expand operations into Bangladesh. The report also warns of Al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates exploring chemical and biological threats and increasingly using cryptocurrencies for terrorist financing.
tweets.content:
UN REPORT LINKS DELHI RED FORT BLAST TO AQIS

A UN Security Council monitoring report has attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi’s Red Fort to Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), adding an international dimension to India’s investigation.

The assessment says AQIS has evolved into a decentralised network of smaller cells, with leadership based in Kabul and efforts to expand operations into Bangladesh.

The report also warns of Al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates exploring chemical and biological threats and increasingly using cryptocurrencies for terrorist financing.

tweets.title: 🇳🇵NEPALESE GORKHAS WANT TO SERVE IN THE INDIAN ARMY AGAIN Former Gorkha soldiers and supporters protested in Pokhara, Nepal, demanding the resumption of recruitment of Nepali youths into the Indian Army under the Agnipath scheme. They argue that joining the Indian Army remains a far better opportunity than low-paid Gulf employment, while also preserving a military tradition that has linked India and Nepal for over two centuries. The protest comes days before Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth’s scheduled five-day visit to Nepal from August 16. Nepal halted Gorkha recruitment under Agnipath amid concerns over the four-year service model and post-service prospects.
tweets.content:
🇳🇵NEPALESE GORKHAS WANT TO SERVE IN THE INDIAN ARMY AGAIN

Former Gorkha soldiers and supporters protested in Pokhara, Nepal, demanding the resumption of recruitment of Nepali youths into the Indian Army under the Agnipath scheme.

They argue that joining the Indian Army remains a far better opportunity than low-paid Gulf employment, while also preserving a military tradition that has linked India and Nepal for over two centuries.

The protest comes days before Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth’s scheduled five-day visit to Nepal from August 16.

Nepal halted Gorkha recruitment under Agnipath amid concerns over the four-year service model and post-service prospects.

tweets.title: A Tribute to Major General Sunil Kumar Razdan, KC, VSM (Retd.)- A Legend of the Indian Army passed away today New Delhi, 13 August 2026 The Indian Defence Forces fraternity mourns the sad demise of Major General Sunil Kumar Razdan, Kirti Chakra, Vishisht Seva Medal, (Retd), a legendary braveheart, an exceptional leader, and an enduring symbol of grit, valour, and indomitable human spirit. An illustrious officer from the 7th Battalion, The Parachute Regiment (7 PARA SF), Major General Razdan carved his name into military history through his extraordinary display of raw courage and selflessness during a counter-terrorist operation in Jammu and Kashmir in 1994. The Heroic Rescue: Tasked with an operation against Lashkar-e-Toiba terrorists holding young women hostage, the then Lt Colonel Razdan led from the front, neutralizing two militants. Despite being critically wounded after taking multiple gunshot wounds to the abdomen that severely injured his spine, he displayed legendary resolve, eliminated the remaining threat, and ensured the safe rescue of the hostages. Refusing immediate evacuation, he remained steadfast until the mission concluded. For his conspicuous gallantry, he was awarded the Kirti Chakra, India's second-highest peacetime gallantry award. Though the severe injuries left him paralyzed below the waist, his unyielding spirit refused to yield to physical constraints. Breaking Barriers: Overcoming his disability with exceptional determination, he broke new ground to become the Indian Army’s first wheelchair-borne General. He continued to serve the nation with distinction, culminating his active service at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), where he conducted stellar and invaluable research. Major General Razdan’s life remains a powerful testament to the highest traditions of the Indian military. His legacy of absolute devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations of soldiers and citizens alike. The nation and the entire fraternity stand in solidarity with his grieving family in this hour of immense sorrow, praying for peace to the departed soul and fortitude to the bereaved family.

A Tribute to Major General Sunil Kumar Razdan, KC, VSM (Retd.)- A Legend of the Indian Army passed away today

New Delhi, 13 August 2026

The Indian Defence Forces fraternity mourns the sad demise of Major General Sunil Kumar Razdan, Kirti Chakra, Vishisht Seva Medal, (Retd), a legendary braveheart, an exceptional leader, and an enduring symbol of grit, valour, and indomitable human spirit. An illustrious officer from the 7th Battalion, The Parachute Regiment (7 PARA SF), Major General Razdan carved his name into military history through his extraordinary display of raw courage and selflessness during a counter-terrorist operation in Jammu and Kashmir in 1994.

The Heroic Rescue: Tasked with an operation against Lashkar-e-Toiba terrorists holding young women hostage, the then Lt Colonel Razdan led from the front, neutralizing two militants. Despite being critically wounded after taking multiple gunshot wounds to the abdomen that severely injured his spine, he displayed legendary resolve, eliminated the remaining threat, and ensured the safe rescue of the hostages. Refusing immediate evacuation, he remained steadfast until the mission concluded. For his conspicuous gallantry, he was awarded the Kirti Chakra, India's second-highest peacetime gallantry award. Though the severe injuries left him paralyzed below the waist, his unyielding spirit refused to yield to physical constraints.

Breaking Barriers: Overcoming his disability with exceptional determination, he broke new ground to become the Indian Army’s first wheelchair-borne General. He continued to serve the nation with distinction, culminating his active service at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), where he conducted stellar and invaluable research.

Major General Razdan’s life remains a powerful testament to the highest traditions of the Indian military. His legacy of absolute devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations of soldiers and citizens alike.

The nation and the entire fraternity stand in solidarity with his grieving family in this hour of immense sorrow, praying for peace to the departed soul and fortitude to the bereaved family.

tweets.title: INDIA IS BUILDING IT'S OWN ASTRONAUT TRAINING HUB ISRO is developing Gaganyatri Nivas and a crew isolation facility at Sriharikota, with a ₹26.02 crore tender floated for planning, design and construction. The facility will train and acclimatise future Indian astronauts, reducing dependence on overseas training. The first Gaganyaan astronaut batch trained in Russia and the US. Future batches could undergo much of their training in India, with facilities inspired by NASA’s mission simulation infrastructure. The bigger vision goes beyond Gaganyaan: a larger astronaut pool, scientific experiments in orbit and eventually India’s Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS). India is building the ecosystem to become a sustained human spaceflight power, not just a one-mission nation.

tweets.title: IAF TO EXPAND ITS TRANSPORT FLEET Defence Ministry has issued an RFP for 60 new transport aircraft for the IAF, in a deal estimated at around $10 billion, according to ThePrint. The aircraft will replace ageing AN-32s and potentially IL-76s, with an option for additional units. Tata Group–Lockheed Martin and Mahindra Defence–Embraer are among the key contenders. The aircraft must support high-altitude operations and unprepared runways, including ALGs in Ladakh and the Northeast. India is also pushing localisation: 40% minimum indigenous content initially, rising to 60% in phases, alongside domestic final assembly and MRO facilities.
tweets.content:
IAF TO EXPAND ITS TRANSPORT FLEET

Defence Ministry has issued an RFP for 60 new transport aircraft for the IAF, in a deal estimated at around $10 billion, according to ThePrint.

The aircraft will replace ageing AN-32s and potentially IL-76s, with an option for additional units.

Tata Group–Lockheed Martin and Mahindra Defence–Embraer are among the key contenders. The aircraft must support high-altitude operations and unprepared runways, including ALGs in Ladakh and the Northeast.

India is also pushing localisation: 40% minimum indigenous content initially, rising to 60% in phases, alongside domestic final assembly and MRO facilities.

tweets.title: R to @NetramDefence: 1931: The Swaraj Flag The year 1931 was a landmark in the history of the flag. A resolution was passed adopting a tricolor flag as the official flag of the Indian National Congress. Design: It featured three horizontal stripes of Saffron (top), White (middle), and Green (bottom). Symbols: Mahatma Gandhi's spinning wheel (Charkha) was placed in the center of the white stripe. tweets.title: RT by @NetramDefence: Nepal has lost the original documents of the 1816 Sugauli Treaty. Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal stated that the government cannot confirm if it possesses the original 1816 Sugauli Treaty. While secondary reference papers exist in the National Archives, extensive searches across state departments failed to locate the definitive, original signed document. The 1816 Sugauli Treaty, signed with British India after the Anglo-Nepal War, is the fundamental legal and historical basis for Nepal's modern territorial claims.
